lessons.title: The First Five Days of Creation
lessons.theme: Creation ex nihilo and the goodness of God's workmanship

days.scriptureTitle: The First Five Days of Creation
days.prayerPoint: Praise God for His great power and goodness.
days.christFocus: John 1:1-3 teaches that Jesus Christ was there in the beginning and that all things were made through Him.

sections.heading: Nothing
sections.text: Have you ever closed your eyes and imagined what it was like before anything was made? There were no trees, no animals, no stars, and no people. There was not even light or dark. There was just nothing at all! But God was there. God has always lived, even before time began.

sections.heading: Poof!
sections.text: God did not need a hammer, nails, or paint to make the world. God simply spoke! He said, 'Let there be light,' and poof—light was made! God separated the light from the darkness. He called the light Day, and the darkness He called Night. That was Day 1.

sections.heading: Shaping
sections.text: On Day 2, God made the sky. He separated the waters above from the waters below. On Day 3, God said, 'Let dry land appear!' The great oceans gathered, and dry ground emerged with green grass, tall trees, and plants of every kind. God saw that it was good.

sections.heading: Missing pieces
sections.text: On Day 4, God put the sun to shine by day and the moon and twinkling stars to shine by night. On Day 5, God filled the waters with splashing sea creatures and the air with singing birds. The earth was quickly filling up with wonder!

questions.prompt: Who created the earth?
questions.explanation: Genesis 1:1 teaches us that in the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.

questions.prompt: What is one thing God created in the first five days?
options: Light, sun, seas, birds, and fish
questions.explanation: During the first five days, God made light, sky, land, plants, sun, moon, stars, sea creatures, and birds!

questions.prompt: Each day, what did God call His work?
questions.explanation: Throughout Genesis 1, God looked at everything He had made and declared that it was good.

activityCard.title: Five Days of Wonders
activityCard.instructions: Take a piece of paper and fold or draw five squares. In each square, draw one wonder God created on that day: 1: Light, 2: Sky, 3: Trees & Land, 4: Sun & Moon, 5: Fish & Birds!

sections.heading: A whole lot of nothing
sections.text: Have you ever wondered why this world is here? Have you ever thought about where everything came from? Before anything in the universe existed, there was God. God did not begin when the universe began; He was already there. When God decided to create the universe, He started with nothing. In Latin, scholars call this creation ex nihilo—creating out of nothing at all.

sections.heading: Nothing to it!
sections.text: Human builders need lumber, bricks, nails, and blueprints to construct a home. But God did not need building materials. Genesis 1 tells us that God spoke, and by the power of His voice, matter, energy, time, and space burst into existence. Psalm 33:6 confirms: 'By the word of the Lord the heavens were made, and all the host of them by the breath of His mouth.'

sections.heading: Nothing but good
sections.text: At each phase of creation, God inspected His work and pronounced it 'good' (tov in Hebrew). When God creates, He establishes order, beauty, function, and purpose. Everything God made reflects His eternal power, divine nature, and boundless goodness.

questions.prompt: How did God create all that exists?
options: By speaking His word out of nothing (ex nihilo)
Using preexisting materials left over in space
questions.explanation: God spoke all of creation into existence out of nothing (ex nihilo) by the power of His word.

questions.prompt: What did God call His creation at each phase?
questions.explanation: God pronounced His creation 'good' (tov in Hebrew), showing its perfection, beauty, and purpose.

questions.prompt: How do we see God's goodness in creation?
options: Through the beauty, order, and provision for living creatures
We cannot see any goodness in the world
questions.explanation: Creation displays God's care, order, and generous provision for every living thing.

focalPoint.title: The Sea in a Jar
supplies: Clear glass jar or bottle with tight lid
Small plastic fish, glitter, or tiny shells
steps: Fill the jar approximately halfway with tap water.
Add two drops of blue food coloring and gently stir until ocean-blue.
Drop in your tiny sea creatures or shells to rest in the water.
Pour vegetable oil or baby oil to fill the rest of the jar.
Tightly secure the lid. Gently tilt the jar back and forth to see the ocean waves roll over the sea creatures God made on Day 5!

days.scriptureTitle: By the Word of the Lord
days.prayerPoint: Praise God for His power and wisdom.
days.christFocus: Jesus Christ is God; all things were made and exist through the Word (John 1; Hebrews 1).

sections.heading: God Spoke and It Was So
sections.text: When you want to build a tower, you have to gather blocks with your hands. But Psalm 33:9 says of God: 'For He spoke, and it was done; He commanded, and it stood fast.' God did not need to break a sweat or borrow tools. His words have ultimate power.

sections.heading: From Messy to Beautiful
sections.text: Before God began shaping the earth, Genesis tells us it was without form and empty. Darkness covered the deep waters. But day by day, God brought light, gave the oceans boundaries, called forth land, and filled the empty skies and waters with creatures.

questions.prompt: How did God create the world?
questions.explanation: Psalm 33:9 tells us: 'He spoke, and it was done.'

questions.prompt: What was the earth like before God shaped it?
questions.explanation: Before God brought order, the earth was formless, empty, and dark.

questions.prompt: How long did God take to make the birds and fish?
options: On Day 5, God spoke them into existence
questions.explanation: On Day 5, God filled the sea with creatures and the sky with winged birds.

activityCard.title: Mini Aquarium Craft
activityCard.instructions: Take a paper plate or clear plastic cup. Color the inside ocean blue. Glue tiny pebbles at the bottom, and draw swimming fish and sea turtles to celebrate God's ocean world!

sections.heading: What Happened in the Beginning
sections.text: The opening words of Scripture anchor everything we believe. God did not emerge from nature; nature came from God. When God created the heavens and the earth, He acted as the supreme Architect and Sovereign King.

sections.heading: God Is Elohim
sections.text: In Genesis 1, the Hebrew name used for God is Elohim. In Hebrew grammar, '-im' is a plural ending. While God is one, this name reflects the majesty, fullness, and three-in-one nature of the Trinity: the Father who decrees, the Son through whom all things are made, and the Spirit who hovered over the face of the waters.

sections.heading: God Sustains
sections.text: Creation is not like a clock that God wound up and walked away from. God actively sustains every heartbeat, every planetary orbit, and every ocean tide. Hebrews 1:3 declares that Jesus upholds all things by the word of His power.

questions.prompt: What does the Hebrew name Elohim mean?
options: The majestic plural name for the all-powerful Creator God
questions.explanation: Elohim is the plural noun of majesty used for the one true God, pointing to the Trinity.

questions.prompt: What did God create in the first five days?
options: Light, sky, land, plants, sun, moon, stars, birds, and sea life
questions.explanation: Days 1-5 established the environments (light, sky, seas/land) and populated them with lights, fish, and birds.

questions.prompt: How does Scripture describe each creation day?
options: The evening and the morning marked each distinct day
questions.explanation: Scripture repeatedly notes: 'So the evening and the morning were the first day... second day...' and so on.

snowmanInteractive.prompt: Did the snowflakes build this by chance?
snowmanInteractive.explanation: When you see a snowman with a carrot nose and button eyes, you know someone made it on purpose. In the same way, the complex order of nature points to the Creator!

days.prayerPoint: Think about God's amazing creation and praise Him.
days.christFocus: Christ is the Creator and Head over all creation (Colossians 1:15-17).

sections.heading: Singing to the Creator
sections.text: Look around at the tall green palm fronds, the jumping dolphins, and the sparkling stars. God made them all because He is generous and good! Everything in creation gives glory to God, and we can join in praising Him with our voices.

questions.prompt: Why do you think God made creation?
options: To show His glory, power, and love
questions.explanation: God created the world to display His glory, wisdom, and goodness to us!

questions.prompt: As God kept working across the days, what happened to the empty earth?
options: God brought perfect order, beauty, and life
questions.explanation: God took what was empty and filled it with light, living creatures, and abundant life.

activityCard.title: Sing the Memory Verse!
activityCard.instructions: Sing Genesis 1:1 to the tune of 'Twinkle, Twinkle Little Star' or 'London Bridge'! Use the in-app melody player below to practice your song.

sections.heading: It All Starts with God
sections.text: When Thomas Edison sought to invent a long-lasting electric light bulb, he tested thousands of different plant fibers and carbon filaments before finding one that worked. Edison was a brilliant inventor, but he had to use materials that God had already created. God alone creates from nothing!

sections.heading: Three Reasons It Matters Who Made the World
sections.text: 1. Identity: You are not an accident of nature; you are purposefully designed by God. 2. Purpose: Because God made everything, creation belongs to Him, and we are responsible to care for it. 3. Trust: The God who spoke the galaxies into being is strong enough to care for you every single day.

sections.heading: Wonder and Worship
sections.text: Psalm 104:24 sings: 'O Lord, how manifold are Your works! In wisdom You have made them all. The earth is full of Your possessions.' When we examine creation, our natural response should be worship.

questions.prompt: What does creation teach us about God?
options: It reveals His eternal power, infinite wisdom, and goodness
That He is far away and does not care
That everything happened randomly without guidance
questions.explanation: Romans 1:20 and Psalm 104 show that God's power and divine nature are clearly seen in creation.

questions.prompt: Why does creation continue to hold together?
options: God actively sustains and upholds all things by His word
Nature runs completely on its own without God
questions.explanation: Scripture teaches that Christ holds all things together by His word of power.

questions.prompt: How should we respond to God's magnificent creation?
options: With wonder, thanksgiving, and joyful worship of the Creator
By worshipping nature instead of God
questions.explanation: We praise and worship the Creator, not the created things.

scriptureConnections.summary: The historical account of the first five days of creation.
Praising the Lord whose spoken word established the universe.
Celebrating God's wisdom, providence, and care over every creature.
Christ is before all things, and in Him all things consist.
All things were made through the Word, and without Him nothing was made.

investigator.speciesCallout: Scientists estimate there are over 8.7 million living species on Earth! Tap the fluttering butterfly swarm over the shore to marvel at God's variety.

days.prayerPoint: Thank God for the life we find in Christ (John 1:4).
days.christFocus: Jesus is both our Creator and our Savior from sin and death.

sections.heading: The Light of the World
sections.text: The Gospel of John tells us something wonderful: Jesus, the Word of God, was with God in the very beginning. Everything that was made was made through Him! Jesus is not only our Savior who loves us, but also our Mighty Creator.

questions.prompt: In today's Scripture, Jesus is called the Word. What was the Word doing when the world began?
options: He was with God, creating all things!
questions.explanation: John 1:3 says: 'All things were made through Him, and without Him nothing was made that was made.'

questions.prompt: If Jesus created the world, what does this tell us about Him?
options: Jesus is truly God and worthy of our worship
He was just a regular man
questions.explanation: Jesus is fully God, the eternal Second Person of the Trinity.

activityCard.title: Name Beautiful Things
activityCard.instructions: Tap things in the 3D scene that you find beautiful (dolphins, coral, sunset, stars). As you tap, release a praise bubble to thank Jesus for making them!

sections.heading: Doctrine: Jesus Was at Creation
sections.text: One of the most foundational truths of the Christian faith is that Jesus Christ is eternal God. John 1:1-3 states: 'In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. He was in the beginning with God. All things were made through Him, and without Him nothing was made that was made.'

sections.heading: Creation and Redemption
sections.text: Why is it important that Jesus was the Creator? Because only the Creator had the power and authority to rescue His fallen creation. The hands that set the stars in their orbits are the very hands that were pierced on the cross for our redemption.

sections.heading: The Alpha and Omega
sections.text: In Revelation 22:13, Jesus announces: 'I am the Alpha and the Omega, the Beginning and the End, the First and the Last.' History began with Him, and all things will be restored under His eternal reign.

questions.prompt: Who is Jesus Christ according to John 1?
options: The eternal Son of God, Creator of all things and our Savior
A wise moral teacher and nothing more
A created angel who helped God
questions.explanation: John 1 teaches that Jesus is the eternal Word who was with God and was God.

questions.prompt: How did God provide redemption for His creation?
options: By sending Jesus Christ to die on the cross and rise again
By erasing the world and starting over
questions.explanation: Jesus, our Creator, came to Earth to bear our sins and bring us eternal life.

questions.prompt: Who controls the universe today?
options: The Lord God Almighty through Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: Christ reigns supreme over all creation, upholding it by His sovereign power.

orangeRiddle.riddle: What has a protective peel, juicy compartments inside, seeds ready to sprout new trees, and never needed a manufacturing plant to design?
orangeRiddle.answer: An orange! God engineered fruit with seeds inside so life would continue to reproduce after its own kind.

days.christFocus: When He calmed the storm (Matthew 8:26), Jesus spoke and creation responded.
